claims.text: The Moon is a thin crescent, twelve percent lit, low in the east — it barely interferes.
Eighty meteors an hour is the rate at the peak itself.
80 meteors an hour at the peak

The Quadrantids peak at 19:37 central Europe time on 3 January 2027, when the radiant in Boötes is barely above the northern horizon here. The practical window is the hours before dawn on 4 January, when the radiant is high in the east. 80 meteors an hour is the peak rate (ZHR); expect a fraction of that by dawn. The Moon is a 12% crescent low in the east and barely interferes.

Positions computed for central Europe (50°N, 15°E) with astronomy-engine; meteor rates from the International Meteor Organization. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
